pr_title: Platform mappings: support setting Starlark flags
pr_body:
In other words, support:

```
platforms:
  //:my_platform
    --//mypkg:my_custom_flag=value
```

#### Non-goals:
 - Refactor the relationship between the Starlark and native option parsers
 - Support Starlark flag -> platform mappings (we could add this if needed but platform mappings isn't a feature we want to expand more than necessary)
 - Parse with simplified ad hoc logic instead of directly using `StarlarkOptionsParser` as the source of truth

#### Approach:
1. The basic problem (described [here](https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/issues/18199#issuecomment-1520620249)) is `StarlarkOptionsParser` needs to convert flag names to `Target`s. `PlatformMappingValue` calls the parsers but can't Skyframe-load `Target`s.
1. So we add support in `PlatformMappingFunction` to Skyframe-load the needed `Target`s
1. But `StarlarkOptionParser` already has code for doing that, outside of a `Skyfunction` environment, through `SkyframeExecutor.loadTargetPatternsWithoutFilters`.
1. So factor out `StarlarkOptionParser`s `Target` loading into an interface the caller can implement
1. The original callers (`BlazeOptionHandler` and `CanonicalizeCommand`) provide the same implementation as before
1. `PlatformMappingFunction` provides a Skyframe retriever through `PackageFunction` (which is a cleaner way to get `Target`s within a `Skyfunction`)

I also had to factor out `StarlarkOptionsParser.java` into its own `java_library` to prevent dependency cycles between `:runtime` and Skyframe: `:runtime` already depends on Skyframe, and by calling `StarlarkOptionsParser` from a Skyfunction that adds a dependency the other way.

Thanks @katre for initial investigation.

Fixes https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/issues/18199.

issue_context.title: platform_mappings files cannot set build flags
issue_context.body:
### Description of the bug:


When trying to set a build flag in a platform_mappings file (using `--//:my_flag="foo"`), bazel gives `ERROR: Unrecognized option: --//:my_flag="foo"`. 

This is something we'd like to use in android until proper new mechanisms are added to manage build settings/flags more easily.


### What's the simplest, easiest way to reproduce this bug? Please provide a minimal example if possible.


Create a directory with an empty `WORKSPACE` file, and then these other files:

BUILD:
```
load(":string_flag.bzl", "string_flag")
load(":write_build_setting.bzl", "write_build_setting")

platform(
    name="my_platform",
)

string_flag(
    name = "my_flag",
    build_setting_default = "",
)

write_build_setting(
    name = "top",
    build_setting = ":my_flag",
)
```

platform_mappings:
```
platforms:
    //:my_platform
        --//:my_flag="Hello from platform_mappings!"
```

string_flag.bzl:
```
BuildSettingInfo = provider(
    doc = "A singleton provider that contains the raw value of a build setting",
    fields = {
        "value": "The value of the build setting in the current configuration. " +
                 "This value may come from the command line or an upstream transition, " +
                 "or else it will be the build setting's default.",
    },
)

def _impl(ctx):
    return BuildSettingInfo(value = ctx.build_setting_value)

string_flag = rule(
    implementation = _impl,
    build_setting = config.string(flag = True),
)
```

write_build_setting.bzl:
```
load(":string_flag.bzl", "BuildSettingInfo")

def _impl(ctx):
    out = ctx.actions.declare_file("out.txt")
    ctx.actions.write(out, ctx.attr.build_setting[BuildSettingInfo].value + "\n")
    return [DefaultInfo(files=depset([out]))]

write_build_setting = rule(
    implementation = _impl,
    attrs = {
        "build_setting": attr.label(),
    },
)
```


Then running `bazel build //:top --platforms=//:my_platform && cat bazel-bin/out.txt` will reproduce the error message.

Running `bazel build //:top --//:my_flag="Hello, world!" && cat bazel-bin/out.txt` works just fine though.


### Which operating system are you running Bazel on?


Linux

### What is the output of `bazel info release`?


Tested on release 6.1.2 and android's ~month old develepment-built version

### If `bazel info release` returns `development version` or `(@non-git)`, tell us how you built Bazel.


_No response_

### What's the output of `git remote get-url origin; git rev-parse master; git rev-parse HEAD` ?


_No response_

### Have you found anything relevant by searching the web?

_No response_

### Any other information, logs, or outputs that you want to share?

_No response_
comments:
Okay, this is quite the rabbithole. I added some simple tests (see https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/pull/18200), and then starting figuring out where to add the support.

It turns out that [`PlatformMappingValue.parse`](https://cs.opensource.google/bazel/bazel/+/master:src/main/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/skyframe/PlatformMappingValue.java?q=symbol%3A%5Cbcom.google.devtools.build.lib.skyframe.PlatformMappingValue.parse%5Cb%20case%3Ayes) creates an [`OptionsParser`](https://cs.opensource.google/bazel/bazel/+/refs/heads/master:src/main/java/com/google/devtools/common/options/OptionsParser.java?q=symbol%3A%5Cbcom.google.devtools.common.options.OptionsParser%5Cb%20case%3Ayes), but what's needed for Starlark option support is a [`StarlarkOptionsParser`](https://cs.opensource.google/bazel/bazel/+/master:src/main/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/runtime/StarlarkOptionsParser.java?q=symbol%3A%5Cbcom.google.devtools.build.lib.runtime.StarlarkOptionsParser%5Cb%20case%3Ayes).

Unfortunately, to [create a `StarlarkOptionsParser`](https://cs.opensource.google/bazel/bazel/+/master:src/main/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/runtime/StarlarkOptionsParser.java?q=symbol%3A%5Cbcom.google.devtools.build.lib.runtime.StarlarkOptionsParser.newStarlarkOptionsParser%5Cb%20case%3Ayes), you need an instance of `CommandEnvironment` (in order to parse and handle arbitrary targets). There isn't one of these available in `PlatformMappingValue`.

We'd probably need to pre-create the parser and pass it into PlatformMappingFunction, so that PlatformMappingValue could use it.
@katre checking in, did you make any progress on the StarlarkOptionsParser issue?

I just prototyped a similar approach to what @katre described (except I recreated the parser directly in `PlatformMappingFunction`).

The implementation is way more technically complicated than I think it should be. But that doesn't have to be the user's concern. 

I'll share a WIP PR tomorrow.
Let us know if you need further adjustments..
